name: Revocation Checker
description: Decide from a CRL whether a certificate is revoked; the CRL signature is verified when the issuer certificate is supplied.

hints.unverified: **No issuer certificate supplied**: the CRL signature was not checked, so this page never claims "not revoked" — it reports "unverified" instead.
hints.order: With an issuer certificate the signature is verified first: a bad signature is an error and no revocation verdict is given.
hints.stale: A stale CRL is always rejected, regardless of the would-be verdict.

faq.q: What is the difference between "unverified" and "not revoked"?
faq.a: "Unverified" only means the certificate is absent from the list; nothing proves the list itself is genuine. "Not revoked" is a verdict reached after the signature checks out.

faq.q: Why is the issuer certificate needed for verification?
faq.a: The CRL is signed by the issuer, so its public key is required to check the signature.

faq.q: What if the CRL has expired?
faq.a: Fetch a fresh CRL; an expired list cannot be used as revocation evidence.
